    How to read the map and route cards
    • Grey route cells: the value is unknown. Unknown is not evidence of a favorable area.
    • Orange cells: a property-value signal below your chosen cutoff, not a safety verdict.
    • Route families: group similar paths to save space. Their sliders do not change ranks or route geometry.
    • Compare: show route families and check any two cards. The map compares that pair automatically. Purple marks exact overlap; nearby parallel roads do not count.
    • Show Exclusion Zones on map: changes visibility only. Hiding them does not remove exclusions from a route search.

      Set the trip

      Applies to returned Valhalla travel time, including all legs. Release the slider to set the limit and discard the previous candidate batch. Known AVM evidence and selected Route Gates are kept.

      Set the absolute-avoid Exclusion Zone level
      How exclusion zones work

      This independent cutoff controls the candidate MUST AVOID zones. The Orange Cell slider remains the more lenient PREFER TO AVOID signal used by normal route ranking. Release this slider to recompute the map preview and the polygons used by the next route batch. Each new batch uses all known qualifying cells within 30 miles of its Start, Destination, and selected gates, whether visible on the current map or not. When Highways or Toll roads is set to Prefer, only the matching road class is masked using the static Valhalla road graph. Known Start and Destination cells below this level are also kept outside Exclusion Zones. A narrow connector may leave a few nearby orange cells outside the hard-avoid polygons so a protected road cell is not accidentally enclosed. Changing this level discards current route candidates and rankings; use Generate fresh route candidates to rebuild from the same Route Gates. Orange-cell colors are unchanged.

      Zone preview uses cells below $200 PPSQFT.

      Enter the street address and ZIP code for each U.S. trip point, then press Enter or Find to place S or D. Address lookup uses the U.S. Census Bureau; check the resulting pin. You can also click the map or enter latitude and longitude. Point names can be edited separately.

      Valhalla can return one primary route and up to three alternatives for the baseline. Gate pair requests use through points and return one route each.

      Valhalla road preferences

      Set these before preparing the route search. They apply to the baseline and every Route Gate combination. Avoid means Valhalla tries another road when possible; it may still use that road to complete a route.

      Unpaved start or end access can still be used. Choose HOV lanes only when your vehicle meets the posted occupancy rules. This search does not use live traffic.

      Required: Shotgun Route Gates
      How the gate search works

      Every new Valhalla search requires reviewed Start Route Gates and Destination Approach Gates. Each selected gate is a through point with a 200 meter road-search radius; it does not guarantee a road within that radius. Once both gate sets are ready, the exact ordered cross-product is prepared and starts automatically when local Valhalla is ready. The search includes every Start × Destination combination, including no gate at either end. With 16 gates at each trip end, that is 17 × 17 = 289 Valhalla requests. GO covers each requested ring with overlapping small circles, merges the road data, and removes duplicates. Completed circles are saved; a failed circle requires an explicit Retry. Preparing gates makes no Valhalla or AVM request.

      Choose an inner radius up to 19 miles and an outer radius up to 20 miles. The outer radius must be greater than the inner radius. These distances apply to the Start and Destination gate rings. Adjust any settings, then select GO. Editing settings does not start a search.

      24 small circles per trip end — up to 48 Census requests for both ends. Saved circles reduce that number. Nothing starts until GO.

      Loading the built-in Chicago starter catalog. After GO, saved circles are reused and missing circles are fetched from Census. No Valhalla or RentCast call is made.

      Coordinates for an uncached area are sent to the U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb service. Successful road data enters the shared cache for reuse. Each circle is about 1 mile in radius, with a 25-second and 5 MiB limit. At most 1,024 circles per trip end, 3 at a time. Failed searches stop; Retry resumes saved progress, with at most 3 attempts per circle.

      SHOTGUN SCREEN REQUIREDScreen and rank the whole candidate pool first

      Every candidate enters the same bounded evidence process before individual route inspection.

      1 Screen and compare every route

      How evidence screening and approval work

      The whole-pool shotgun screen is required before route inspection or choice. Choose how many unknown, eligible route cells to sample for each enabled route. Known eligible AVM cells are the initial anchors. If any are known, the next unknown cell is farthest from the nearest anchor; with no known values, a one-cell quota targets the unknown midpoint and larger quotas start with the earliest and latest unknowns before spreading. The same rule applies to the initial screen and every additional round. Use each ranking card to include or exclude that route from future evidence rounds; excluded routes stay in the ranking. Shared cells count once and update every route containing them. The ranking is advisory. Every missing or failed lookup stays unknown; failed attempts count against the route quota. Requests run within a bounded plan with no retries, and you still inspect the routes and choose. The free cache check produces the exact cell-request count and route list first. You review that count and select Approve before any AVM request is sent. Orange means below $200 PPSQFT, a geographic value signal rather than a safety measure.

      Set the PPSQFT map color bounds

      Release the Orange lower-bound slider to recolor AVM cells and rerank the existing routes using their current evidence. Apply also recalculates Orange miles, Orange Percent, and the ranking. Existing candidates and Route Gates are kept; no route or AVM lookup is sent.

      Choose and apply the Orange Cell level before the first Route Ranking.

      The slider uses a logarithmic PPSQFT scale so small and large bounds are both reachable. Orange through blue spreads between the displayed lower and upper bounds. Releasing this slider changes map colors only; it does not rerank routes or request AVM values.

      Map colors span $200 to $500 PPSQFT.

      Travel time / Orange Miles tradeoff

      Score = travel minutes + 3 × estimated Orange Miles. Lowest score wins. Unknown miles use the same Orange percentage as known miles.

      0 favors the shortest time. Higher values favor avoiding Orange Miles. Changes rerank existing routes immediately.

      Changed the Exclusion Cutoff?

      Changing the Exclusion Cutoff discards the current candidate batch and requires fresh routes from the same selected Start and Destination Route Gates. Changing Orange PPSQFT reranks the existing routes without requesting new candidates.

      Select and review both Route Gate sets to enable fresh route generation.

      This count starts at 5. The first ranking checks saved evidence without new paid lookups. For each later round, choose up to this many unknown, eligible cells per INCLUDED route. Toggle route eligibility on each ranking card. Shared cells are requested once and update every route containing them; routes with fewer eligible cells receive fewer. Calculate the exact lookup count. After the free cache check, review the exact number of unique cell requests; no AVM request is sent until you approve. The deduplicated plan is capped at 100 calls; failures count and no retries occur. Set 0 to use only existing evidence.

      If the final deduplicated plan exceeds 100 unique calls, lower the per-route count or disable routes.

      Selection is deterministic: known eligible AVM cells and newly selected cells are anchors. With known values, each next cell is farthest from its nearest anchor. Without known values, one requested cell targets the unknown midpoint; larger quotas seed the eligible unknown endpoints and then spread by distance. Shared selected cells are requested once.

      The first ranking checks saved evidence without paid lookups. Round 0 starts with a 35% cutoff and keeps every route with under 20% known coverage. You can change the cutoff for each later round in the ranking review. Each later round waits for your approval after the exact lookup count and cell list are frozen.
      AVM lookup forecast will appear after route cells and the shared cache are checked. This check makes no new RentCast request.

        3 Inspect a ranked route
        Inspect orange cells with Street View before choosing your route.
        

        How scores and coverage work
        Routes with known eligible evidence rank by travel minutes + the selected minutes per Orange Mile × estimated Orange miles. The lowest score wins. Estimated Orange miles = known Orange miles + unknown miles × (known Orange miles / all known eligible miles). The cards report estimates and known Orange evidence separately. At 0, travel time decides. Equal scores use shorter travel time, then lower Orange Percent, then higher coverage. Routes without known eligible evidence remain unranked. Known Exclusion Zone Miles Under uses the independent Exclusion cutoff; that constraint remains unchanged.
        Known cell values are weighted by non-highway route distance. Valhalla highway maneuvers and attached ramps are excluded. Missing values reduce coverage and remain unknown. Orange means below your $200 per-square-foot cutoff; it is a geographic value signal, not a measured safety rating.
        The Chicago grid uses 1 km center spacing and fixed cell-center AVM queries. Street View inspection uses a point on your route. Standard subject: single-family home, 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, 1,500 sq ft.
        Saved Route 5 exposure-time aggregates are historical and are not recalculated. Fresh route evaluations show distance and coverage using your cutoff.

Map notes · zone details and route statistics

          Zone membership: Interior white pockets are still inside the Exclusion Zone. White means the underlying cells are non-Orange or unmapped; it does not mean those areas are outside the zone. When Highways or Toll roads is set to Prefer, matching road cells are also kept outside by a narrow connector that can leave nearby orange cells outside the hard-avoid area. New Valhalla batches receive these polygons. Prepared batches keep the exclusions they already froze.
          

          Valhalla MUST AVOID zones use the independent Exclusion Zone level. This map shows the visible area. New batches also use qualifying known cells within 30 miles of their Start, Destination, and selected gates, even outside this map view.
          

          

          Evidence, not a safety verdict. AVM values describe a geographic value signal. Street View adds your visual assessment.
